title: Never run the ABACUS/LibRPA symmetry lane with SOC, and keep it off for molecules and Gamma-only cases
symptom: The periodic-GW symmetry lane was being applied to workflows where it is not valid: SOC (`nspin=4` spinor) calculations and molecular (Gamma-only) RPA calculations.
root_cause: The symmetry consumption lane (ABACUS EXX symmetry sidecars plus LibRPA `use_abacus_exx_symmetry` / `use_abacus_gw_symmetry`, and the k-star/spinor rotation machinery) is only validated for non-SOC periodic solids; the molecular lane has no k-star structure to exploit and uses a different reference recipe.
minimal_fix: SOC: keep ABACUS `symmetry = -1` and leave the LibRPA symmetry flags off - the rule was written into README.md, skills/oh-my-librpa/SKILL.md, skills/oh-my-librpa/references/gw-route.md and as comments in the INPUT_scf and librpa.in templates (commit `8f81db1 Clarify SOC symmetry and LibRI provenance`). Molecules (companion recipe, session rollout-2026-05-18T16-55-42-019e3a4c-5755-7560-b096-28f6b3b30034.jsonl): use `symmetry = 0`, set `exx_ccp_rmesh_times` equal to `rpa_ccp_rmesh_times`, skip the NSCF and PyATB stages entirely, and write `librpa.in` without symmetry and without head/wing.
validation: Read the ABACUS log for the actual `nspin` and nks before trusting any symmetry benchmark; for molecules confirm EXX and RPA use the same rmesh factor and that no symmetry/head-wing keys are present in `librpa.in`.
avoid: Do not enable LibRPA symmetry merely because ABACUS accepted `symmetry=1`; the lane is version- and case-dependent (SOC, molecules, metals with Drude head, and head/wing each have separate rules), and the symmetry flags must be consistent between INPUT_scf and librpa.in.
